correctness.rationale: For any compact invariant probability measure, invariance gives zero integral for each smooth coboundary. The identities follow exactly from \(\dot x=y^2(\kappa y^{2r-1}-1)\) and \(d(cy-z)/dt=ac z^2-bx^2\). The support-crossing argument exhausts the only zeros \(y=0\) and \(y=h\) and checks that invariant trajectories on either constant level are equilibria. The conditional RMS bound is monotonicity of \(L^p\) norms on a probability space, with its equality case carried through the invariant-level argument. The source substitutions \(ac/b=6/11\) and \(ac/b=1\) were checked exactly.

value.rationale: The source is explicitly about amplitude control, so an exact parameter-level recurrence threshold is directly motivated rather than an arbitrary slice. The theorem upgrades selected numerical amplitude curves to constraints on every compact recurrent statistical state. It identifies a nontrivial qualitative feature—mandatory overshoot of the nominal control level—and, for SL8III, a parameter-independent exact RMS equality between \(x\) and \(z\). These facts are useful as consistency checks for simulations and for understanding what the control parameter can and cannot constrain.
